prompt:
Find what the PostgreSQL Global Development Group officially states about how long each major PostgreSQL version receives fixes. Cite the official versioning policy page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The official PostgreSQL versioning policy states that each major version is supported for five years after its initial release, during which time it receives bug fixes and security fixes via minor releases.

SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/?from_the_consensus=1 | QUOTE: "The PostgreSQL Global Development Group supports a major version for 5 years after its initial release." | CLAIM: Each major PostgreSQL version receives support (including fixes) for 5 years after its initial release.
SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/?from_the_consensus=1 | QUOTE: "Each major version receives bug fixes and, if need be, security fixes that are released at least once every three months in what we call a "minor release."" | CLAIM: During the supported period, each major version receives bug fixes and security fixes via minor releases at least quarterly.
SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/?from_the_consensus=1 | QUOTE: "After this, a final minor version will be released and the software will then be unsupported (end-of-life)." | CLAIM: After the 5-year support period ends, a final minor version is released and the software becomes unsupported.
